claim: Doxorubicin is widely used for the treatment of solid tumors and hematologic malignancies.
source: Anthracyclines, such as doxorubicin (Dox), are widely used chemotherapeutic agents for the treatment of solid tumors and hematologic malignancies.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about doxorubicin's clinical use.

claim: Doxorubicin frequently induces cardiotoxicity leading to dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure.
source: However, they frequently induce cardiotoxicity leading to dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known side effect of doxorubicin treatment.

claim: Doxorubicin induces DNA damage in cardiomyocytes.
source: We show that Dox induces DNA damage and cardiomyocyte cell death with apoptotic features.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including H2AX phosphorylation measurements.

claim: Doxorubicin induces cardiomyocyte cell death with apoptotic features.
source: We show that Dox induces DNA damage and cardiomyocyte cell death with apoptotic features.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing caspase activation, mitochondrial membrane permeabilization, and other apoptotic markers.

claim: Doxorubicin leads to an increase in cAMP concentration.
source: Dox also led to an increase in both cAMP concentration and EPAC1 activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental measurements of cAMP concentration shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Doxorubicin leads to an increase in EPAC1 activity.
source: Dox also led to an increase in both cAMP concentration and EPAC1 activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from pull-down assays and BRET sensor measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of EPAC1 with CE3F4 alleviated the whole Dox-induced pattern of alterations.
source: The pharmacological inhibition of EPAC1 (with CE3F4) but not EPAC2 alleviated the whole Dox-induced pattern of alterations.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing CE3F4 reduced DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cell death.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of EPAC2 did not alleviate Dox-induced alterations.
source: The pharmacological inhibition of EPAC1 (with CE3F4) but not EPAC2 alleviated the whole Dox-induced pattern of alterations.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing ESI-05 (EPAC2 inhibitor) did not protect against Dox-induced effects.

claim: Dox-treated wild type mice developed dilated cardiomyopathy.
source: When administered in vivo, Dox-treated WT mice developed a dilated cardiomyopathy which was totally prevented in EPAC1 knock-out (KO) mice.
evidence: This is supported by echocardiographic data showing decreased ejection fraction and increased left ventricle end-diastolic volume in WT mice.

claim: Dilated cardiomyopathy was totally prevented in EPAC1 knock-out mice.
source: When administered in vivo, Dox-treated WT mice developed a dilated cardiomyopathy which was totally prevented in EPAC1 knock-out (KO) mice.
evidence: This is supported by echocardiographic data showing preserved cardiac function in EPAC1 KO mice after Dox treatment.

claim: EPAC1 inhibition potentiated Dox-induced cell death in several human cancer cell lines.
source: Moreover, EPAC1 inhibition potentiated Dox-induced cell death in several human cancer cell lines.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing increased cell death in MCF-7 and HeLa cells when treated with Dox plus CE3F4.

claim: EPAC1 inhibition appears as a potential therapeutic strategy to limit Dox-induced cardiomyopathy without interfering with its antitumoral activity.
source: Thus, EPAC1 inhibition appears as a potential therapeutic strategy to limit Dox-induced cardiomyopathy without interfering with its antitumoral activity.
evidence: This is based on inference from the combined data showing cardioprotection and enhanced anticancer effects.

claim: Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity can be acute with immediate cardiac disorders (arrhythmias).
source: Dox cardiotoxicity can be acute with immediate cardiac disorders (arrhythmias) or chronic with remodeling cardiomyopathies (dilated cardiomyopathy [DCM], heart failure [HF]) years after treatment (Lipshultz et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lipshultz et al., 2010.

claim: Doxorubicin cardiotoxicity can be chronic with remodeling cardiomyopathies years after treatment.
source: Dox cardiotoxicity can be acute with immediate cardiac disorders (arrhythmias) or chronic with remodeling cardiomyopathies (dilated cardiomyopathy [DCM], heart failure [HF]) years after treatment (Lipshultz et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lipshultz et al., 2010.

claim: Doxorubicin is a DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor.
source: Mechanistically, Dox, a DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor, induces DNA double strand break by direct DNA interaction (L'Ecuyer et al., 2006), oxidative stress (Cappetta et al., 2017; Rochette et al., 2015), and decreased ATP production (Tokarska-Schlattner et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about doxorubicin's mechanism of action.

claim: Doxorubicin induces DNA double strand breaks by direct DNA interaction.
source: Mechanistically, Dox, a DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor, induces DNA double strand break by direct DNA interaction (L'Ecuyer et al., 2006), oxidative stress (Cappetta et al., 2017; Rochette et al., 2015), and decreased ATP production (Tokarska-Schlattner et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to L'Ecuyer et al., 2006.

claim: DNA damage and heart failure are prevented in cardiac-specific topoisomerase IIβ knock-out mice.
